method: OPEN AND QUOTED from Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3) 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)' (published 31 August 2024). Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at NCBI PMC efetch JATS <license> element for PMC11466906 (Europe PMC returned HTTP 503 on 2026-09-23)).

claims.claim: **HPV is found in around 99% of cervical cancers.** Early disease is often silent, so screening matters; abnormal cytology or a positive high-risk HPV test leads to colposcopy and biopsy.
claims.source_text: HPV, and the oncogenic subtypes HPV16 and 18 in particular, is detected in around 99% of cervical tumors. … Early CC is frequently asymptomatic, underscoring the importance of screening. Abnormal cervical cytology or a positive high-risk HPV test should prompt the performance of colposcopy and biopsy, or excisional procedures such as loop electrosurgical excision and conization.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Locally advanced disease can cause abnormal bleeding or discharge, pelvic pain and dyspareunia,** easily mistaken for vaginitis or cervicitis. Bowel or urinary symptoms or fistula suggest advanced disease.
claims.source_text: Locally advanced CC (LACC) may cause abnormal vaginal bleeding or discharge, pelvic pain, and dyspareunia. These symptoms are non-specific and may be mistaken for vaginitis or cervicitis. … Bowel or urinary symptoms, such as pressure-related complaints, hematuria, hematochezia, or the passage of urine or stool through the vagina, are uncommon and point toward advanced disease
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A visible or palpable lesion is diagnosed by biopsy;** examine under anaesthesia if pelvic examination is inadequate or vaginal or parametrial spread is uncertain.
claims.source_text: If a gross palpable lesion is present, diagnosis is based on biopsy. If a thorough pelvic examination cannot be carried out or there is uncertainty regarding vaginal/parametrial involvement, it should preferably be conducted under anesthesia
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage with FIGO 2018, which now includes imaging and pathology.** Use pelvic MRI for local extent and PET/CT for stage IB3 and above (chest and abdominal CT if PET is unavailable). Cystoscopy or proctoscopy only if invasion is suspected.
claims.source_text: However, the latest FIGO update in 2018 incorporates imaging and pathology findings to improve the prognostic correlation and better tailor treatment … Recommended radiological imaging include pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to evaluate local disease extension (preferred for FIGO stage IB1-IB3). Additionally, positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) in early stages with suspicious lymph nodes (LN) or locally advanced tumors (EIB3 and higher) is recommended to assess nodal and distant disease. If PET/CT is not available, chest and abdominal CT can be used instead [II, B]. … Cystoscopy and proctoscopy are only recommended if bladder or rectal invasion is suspected [IV, D].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Para-aortic node dissection may be considered when imaging shows no para-aortic disease,** to find occult metastases that would change the radiotherapy field.
claims.source_text: Therefore, PALN dissection may be considered to reduce the risk of undetected occult metastases when imaging shows no PALN involvement [II, B].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Five-year survival is about 60% for locally advanced disease,** under 50% with pelvic node metastases and under 20–30% with para-aortic node metastases.
claims.source_text: According to the SEER database 2022, the 5-year survival rates are 91% for early stages, 60% for locally advanced stages … Five-year survival is < 50% in patients with pelvic LN metastasis and < 20-30% in those with PALN metastasis.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Locally advanced means FIGO IB2, II, III and IVA. Standard treatment is external beam radiotherapy with weekly cisplatin, then brachytherapy;** it adds about 10% to overall survival and halves relapse risk. Weekly carboplatin AUC2 is the alternative in renal impairment.
claims.source_text: Locally advanced disease is defined as FIGO stages IB2, II, III, and IVA. Radical treatment with EBRT and weekly cisplatin followed by brachytherapy has demonstrated benefit in five, phase 3 trials, as well as in a Cochrane meta-analysis []. This approach results in a 10% increase in OS and a 50% decrease in the risk of relapse and is the current standard of care [I, A]. The alternative in case of renal impairment could be weekly carboplatin AUC2.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Weekly cisplatin dose: 40 mg/m², capped at 70 mg a week.**
claims.source_text: The cisplatin dosage for this schedule is 40 mg/m2 per week, with a 70-mg weekly limit based on other concurrent trials in locally advanced disease. … Primary weekly cisplatin-based (40 mg/m2) CRT remains the standard of care for LACC until immunotherapy is approved [I, A].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pembrolizumab with chemoradiation (KEYNOTE-A18)** for high-risk disease (FIGO 2014 IB2–IIB node-positive, or III–IVA) improved progression-free survival (HR 0.70) and 24-month survival (87% vs 81%). The guideline expects it to become standard.
claims.source_text: The KEYNOTE-A18 study has recently been published that examined the efficacy of adding pembrolizumab to standard CRT in patients with high-risk, locally advanced CC (FIGO 2014 stage IB2-IIB with node-positive disease or stage III-IVA). The results revealed an increase in PFS with a HR 0.70 (0.55-0.89, p = 0.0020) and 24-month OS of 87% in the pembrolizumab-chemoradiotherapy group and 81% in the placebo-chemoradiotherapy group. … The addition of pembrolizumab to CRT will likely become the standard treatment for LACC [I, A].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Induction chemotherapy (INTERLACE: 6 weekly carboplatin AUC 2 plus paclitaxel 80 mg/m² before chemoradiation)** is an option for selected patients.
claims.source_text: The GCIG INTERLACE trial randomized 500 IB1 node positive, IB2, II, IIIB, and IVA (FIGO 2008) patients to 6 cycles of weekly carboplatin (AUC 2) and paclitaxel (80 mg/m2) before CRT versus CRT alone. … Induction chemotherapy with the INTERLACE regimen before definitive CRT might be an option for selected patients [I, B].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not give adjuvant chemotherapy after chemoradiation, and do not use neoadjuvant chemotherapy before radical surgery** as a standard.
claims.source_text: Adjuvant ChT after CRT is not recommended [I, D]. Neoadjuvant ChT before radical surgery is not a standard approach in LACC [I, D].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After radical surgery with high-risk findings** (positive nodes, margins or parametrium), give pelvic radiotherapy with concurrent platinum.
claims.source_text: If positive pelvic LN, positive surgical margins, and/or positive parametrium are identified, postoperative pelvic EBRT with concurrent platinum-containing ChT is recommended.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Up to 70% of locally advanced cancers recur, mostly within two years.** Confirm recurrence histologically. Central pelvic recurrence without sidewall, extrapelvic nodal or peritoneal disease: pelvic exenteration in a specialised centre.
claims.source_text: The risk of recurrence ranges from 16 to 30% in early stages and up to 70% in LACC. Most relapses occur within the first two years after diagnosis … Patients suspected of recurrent disease require a thorough diagnostic work-up and the recurrence should be histologically confirmed. … Pelvic exenteration is recommended for central pelvic recurrence where there is no involvement of the pelvic sidewall, extrapelvic nodes, or peritoneal disease [IV, B].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Metastatic or recurrent disease:** platinum–paclitaxel plus pembrolizumab for fit patients with PD-L1 CPS 1 or more, with bevacizumab once fistula risk is discussed; cemiplimab after platinum if no prior immunotherapy.
claims.source_text: Platinum-based ChT combined with pembrolizumab is recommended for medically fit patients with recurrent/metastatic PD-L1 positive CC, assessed as CPS of 1 or more [I, A]. … The addition of bevacizumab is recommended when the risk of significant gastrointestinal/genitourinary fistula has been carefully assessed and discussed with the patient [I, A]. … Patients who progress after first-line platinum-based ChT and have not yet received immunotherapy should be offered cemiplimab, regardless of PD-L1 tumor status [I, A]
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Image high-risk stage II+ patients 3–6 months after treatment** (PET/CT preferred, plus pelvic MRI). Then review every 3–6 months for two years and every 6–12 months in years 3–5, with specialist vaginal and pelvic-rectal examination; return to annual checks after five recurrence-free years.
claims.source_text: For high-risk patients with stage II or greater, CT or PET/CT (preferred) and pelvic MRI (recommended), should be performed within 3-6 months of completing therapy. … A reasonable follow-up schedule involves visits every 3-6 months during the first two years and every 6-12 months during years 3-5. … Patients should return to annual population-based general physical and pelvic examinations after five years of recurrence-free follow-up
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Routine cytology after chemoradiation has low predictive value.** Teach patients recurrence symptoms, and start vaginal dilators with lubricant and topical oestrogen early for sexual rehabilitation.
claims.source_text: Systematic cervical and/or vaginal cytology after CRT or surgery has a low positive predictive value for detecting recurrence. … Following treatment, patients should be educated about signs/symptoms suggestive of recurrence as a relevant part of the surveillance plan. … Early use of vaginal dilators concurrent with lubricants and topical estrogen is recommended for suitable sexual rehabilitation.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Ovarian Cancer Research Group (GEICO), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03604-3), 'SEOM-GEICO Clinical Guidelines on cervical cancer (2023)', published 31 August 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11466906/, retrieved 2026-09-23
